ideas.a: It gets rid of by-products of the body's own chemical reactions (not undigested food)
Examples are urea, carbon dioxide and excess salts and water
The kidneys, lungs and skin do it

model: When the body gets harmful by-products of its own chemical reactions, such as urea and carbon dioxide, out through the kidneys, lungs and skin.

ideas.a: Keeping the concentration of the body fluids steady (not too dilute, not too concentrated)
The kidneys do most of it, under the control of ADH; it is part of homeostasis
It matches what is taken in (drinking, food) with what is lost (urine, sweat, breath)

model: Keeping the concentration of the body fluids steady, so they are not too dilute or too concentrated. The kidneys do most of it.

ideas.a: One of about a million tiny tubes in each kidney: its basic working part
It is made of Bowman's capsule (with the glomerulus), the coiled tubules and the loop of Henle
Urine is made in it, by filtration and then reabsorption

model: One of about a million tiny tubes in each filtering organ. Starting at Bowman's capsule and running through the loop of Henle, it is where urine is made.

ideas.a: A knot or ball of tiny vessels
Sits inside Bowman's capsule, at the start of a nephron
Small substances are forced out of it under high pressure (its outgoing arteriole is narrower)

model: A tiny knot of vessels sitting in Bowman's capsule, where high pressure forces water and small molecules out.

ideas.a: A hollow, double-walled cup that wraps around the glomerulus (the knot of vessels)
It collects the fluid forced out of the blood (water, glucose, urea and salts)
It is the first part of the nephron, in the cortex

model: The hollow, double-walled start of each nephron. It wraps around the knot of vessels and collects the fluid forced out of the blood.

ideas.a: All the glucose and amino acids (the useful molecules) are taken back into the blood here
By active transport, which uses energy
Its cells have microvilli (large surface area) and many mitochondria
The coiled tube straight after Bowman's capsule

model: Coiled tube just after Bowman's capsule. Its cells, with microvilli and many mitochondria, take back all the sugar and useful molecules by active transport.

ideas.a: A U-shaped bend in the nephron that dips down and comes back up (two limbs)
It pumps out salts, making the tissue around it (the medulla) very salty
So water leaves the tubule by osmosis and is reabsorbed (longer loops in desert animals save more)

model: A U-shaped bend of the tube dipping deep into the kidney. It pumps out salt so the tissue around it is very salty and water leaves the tube by osmosis.

ideas.a: The tubule after the loop of Henle, just before the collecting duct
It is coiled and lies in the cortex
Water (and some salts) are reabsorbed here, controlled by ADH from the pituitary

model: Coiled tube in the cortex after the loop of Henle and before the collecting duct, where the pituitary hormone controls how much water is taken back.

ideas.a: Many nephrons (their DCTs) drain into it
It runs down through the medulla (a pyramid) to the pelvis
ADH controls how much water it takes back: the last place water is reabsorbed

model: The final tube that many nephrons drain into. It runs down through the medulla, and the pituitary hormone sets how much water it takes back.

ideas.a: A hormone made by the hypothalamus and released by the pituitary gland (in the brain)
More is released when the blood is too concentrated (you're short of water)
It makes the collecting ducts more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed
So a small volume of concentrated urine is made

model: Released by a gland under the brain when the blood is too concentrated. It makes the kidney tubes let more water back into the blood, so less urine is made.

ideas.a: Breaking down spare amino acids (from protein we don't need)
The nitrogen-containing (amine) group is taken off
It makes urea, which the kidneys excrete in urine

model: Breaking down spare protein building blocks by removing their nitrogen part, which makes a waste that the kidneys pass out in urine.

ideas.a: It branches off the aorta, the main artery from the heart
Its blood is rich in oxygen and still full of urea
It brings the blood into the kidney to be filtered

model: It branches off the main vessel from the heart and brings an oxygen-rich supply, still full of urea, into the organ to be filtered.

ideas.a: It takes the blood out of the kidney, back towards the heart (to the vena cava)
Its blood has the least urea in the body: it has just been cleaned
Its blood is deoxygenated (low in oxygen)

model: Carries the cleaned, deoxygenated supply, now with the least urea, out of the organ and back to the heart via the vena cava.

ideas.a: It carries urine away from the kidney (from its pelvis)
Down to the bladder, where urine is stored
There are two, one from each kidney
Muscle in its wall pushes the urine along (peristalsis)

model: One of two muscular ducts that carry urine from the pelvis of each filtering organ down to the stretchy bag where it is stored.

ideas.a: A stretchy, muscular sac
It holds urine until it is let out
The ureters fill it and the urethra empties it

model: A stretchy, muscular sac low in the abdomen that holds the waste liquid from the ureters until you let it out.

ideas.a: It carries urine out of the body
From the bladder, where urine is stored
A ring of muscle (sphincter) controls when it opens
In males it also carries sperm, through the penis

model: Carries urine from the storage bag out to the outside world, through a ring of muscle; in males it also carries sperm through the penis.
